294:
Blancaflor P. Arada’s study investigates the effectiveness of Discord as a communication and collaboration tool for Bachelor of Arts in Multimedia Studies (BAMS) students at the University of the Philippines Open University. Using a mixed-methods approach and a descriptive research design, the study collected data from 238 students to examine the relationships between social presence, interaction, collaboration, and satisfaction through the lens of the Community of Inquiry model, Social Presence Theory, and Collaborative Learning Theory.

The findings indicate that Discord significantly enhances social presence, with 84% of students feeling more connected to peers and faculty. Real-time chat, voice discussions, and multimedia sharing helped create a stronger sense of community than traditional Learning Management Systems. Regarding social interaction, 71% of students reported frequent engagement, primarily through text chat (95%), voice discussions (60%), and direct messaging (50%). Additionally, 65% of students noted that the platform facilitated collaborative learning through knowledge sharing and problem-solving. Overall, 64% of students expressed satisfaction, citing improved faculty communication (86%) and peer interaction (69%).

Challenges included varying levels of technical familiarity, preferences for other platforms, and the underutilization of certain channels. The platform's effectiveness also depended on peer engagement levels. The study concludes that Discord is an effective supplementary tool for reducing isolation in online learning, though it recommends onboarding tutorials and informal activities to maximize community cohesion.
